headline.purpose: The product name in the brand block. The only h1 in the application; the largest type anywhere in the chrome.

title.purpose: Section headings inside panes — Runtime, Session. Sits within the chrome rather than above it.

body.purpose: Message text and empty-state copy. pre-wrap so the model's line breaks survive.

label.purpose: The workhorse: status bar, version, role tags, tree and console headers. Uppercased where it labels a region.

micro.purpose: Progress percentages, tool-card metadata, run statistics. Almost always a number, always tabular.

nano.purpose: The type floor: count badges, menu group labels, file-size readouts. Never set below weight 650.

code.purpose: Editor content, console output, tool code, raw model stream. Size tracks how much of it you are expected to read.

shadows.name: signal-glow
shadows.purpose: Cyan halo on the mote mark and the brand symbol core. Means the runtime is live — never atmosphere.

shadows.name: status-halo
shadows.purpose: Readout-scale glow under a ready status dot. Takes the dot's own color, so an idle dot glows grey.

shadows.name: inset-selected
shadows.purpose: 1px cyan left edge marking the selected file. A border drawn where a real border would shift layout.

shadows.name: inset-active
shadows.purpose: 1px cyan bottom edge marking the active segment in the preview-width control.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: focus-visible ring on every interactive control, paired with a solid border shift.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Default for hover and focus. Color and shadow only — geometry never transitions.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Active state on buttons, applied instantly with no transition. Excluded on menu triggers.

motion.name: spin
motion.purpose: The only keyframe animation in the host application: loading and generating indicators.

motion.name: progress-fill
motion.value: width, set inline per progress report
motion.purpose: The load bar's inner span. Written directly, not animated — layout properties must not be transitioned here.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The only cyan fill on screen. One per region, usually Load model.

components.css: .ds-tabs { display: flex; gap: 0.25rem; padding-bottom: 0.65rem; } .ds-tab { position: relative; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.45rem; height: 2.2rem; padding: 0 0.8rem; color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.65 0.015 240)); background: transparent; border: 0; cursor: pointer; font: 560 0.75rem/1 "Inter Variable", sans-serif; } .ds-tab svg { width: 0.85rem; height: 0.85rem; } .ds-tab:hover { color: var(--foreground, oklch(0.94 0.012 235)); } .ds-tab:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ring, oklch(0.73 0.14 183)); outline-offset: -2px; } .ds-tab.is-active { color: var(--foreground, oklch(0.94 0.012 235)); } .ds-tab.is-active::after { position: absolute; right: 0.8rem; bottom: -0.65rem; left: 0.8rem; height: 1px; content: ""; background: var(--primary, oklch(0.82 0.16 183)); } .ds-badge { display: inline-grid; min-width: 1.15rem; height: 1.05rem; padding: 0 0.3rem; place-items: center; color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.65 0.015 240)); background: var(--muted, oklch(0.19 0.01 255)); border-radius: 999px; font: 650 0.62rem/1 "Inter Variable", sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-badge--error { color: oklch(0.12 0.02 28); background: oklch(0.73 0.16 28); }

narrative.overview:
Mote looks like a bench instrument in a dark lab. It is unlabeled until you know it, dense with readouts, and honest about its own state at all times. Nothing is explained; everything is displayed. The surface is a near-black graphite with a faint blue cast, ruled into panels by hairline borders, and the only color in the room is a single cyan that means this is live. Numbers are everywhere — VRAM, bytes, tokens per second, console counts, percentages — and they are set in tabular figures so they tick in place instead of jittering.

The density is deliberate and high. Type runs small (0.62–1rem across the entire application; there is no display type anywhere in the chrome), letter-spacing on labels is opened up to 0.055em so they stay legible at that size, and structural padding rarely exceeds 1rem. This is an interface for someone who already knows what the controls do. Affordance comes from precision and immediate response, not from generous hit areas or explanatory color.

The one thing the design must never do is look like an AI product. There are no purple gradients, no sparkles, no robot or brain imagery, and no friendly-assistant framing anywhere in the system — this is a standing brand commitment, not a stylistic preference. Mote is infrastructure: a runtime, a debugger, a piece of machinery small enough to fit in a tab. The cyan is not a brand color being applied decoratively; it is a lamp, and lamps mean something.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-only. color-scheme: dark is set at the root; there is no light theme and no toggle.
One accent, used sparingly, always meaning "live" or "selected".
Flat by construction — no drop shadows anywhere; depth is four tonal surface steps and 1px borders.
Every number is tabular; every measurement is visible.
Monospace is reserved for code, logs, paths, and measurements — never for decoration.

rules.name: The Single Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Cyan marks exactly one thing per region: what is live, or what is selected. If two elements in the same pane are cyan, one of them is wrong. Its rarity is the entire reason it reads as a lamp.

rules.name: The Two Reds Rule
rules.body: Alert Red (oklch(0.68 0.2 25)) is for actions you can take — destructive buttons, inline delete confirmations, error banners you must respond to. Log Red (oklch(0.73 0.16 28)) is for things that already happened — console output, failed tool calls, error counts. They are close enough to be mistaken for each other and must never be swapped.

rules.name: The Cool Axis Rule
rules.body: Every neutral sits at hue 235–255 with chroma ≤0.015. A neutral warmer than that, or more saturated, breaks the read that the cyan is the only real color in the room.

rules.name: The Monospace Is Evidence Rule
rules.body: Monospace means the characters matter individually: source code, console output, file paths, and run_js snippets. It is never used for headings, labels, buttons, or atmosphere. A monospace heading would make Mote look like a product imitating a terminal instead of being an instrument.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change in place gets font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums — progress percentages, byte counts, VRAM, tokens per second, file sizes, console counts, timestamps, the version. A readout that reflows while it updates is a broken readout.

rules.name: The Small-And-Tracked Rule
rules.body: Below 0.7rem, letter-spacing opens to 0.055em and weight rises to 650. Small type in this system is dense on purpose, never faint: reach for tracking and weight before reaching for a larger size.

rules.name: The Nothing-Below-The-Fold Rule
rules.body: Every grid row that contains a scroll container declares min-height: 0, and every flexible track is minmax(0, 1fr), never bare 1fr. A grid item's automatic minimum is its content, so without this the message list pushes the composer off screen as the conversation grows and the action bar widens the page on mobile. This is not a preference — it is the reason the layout works.

rules.name: The Glow Means Alive Rule
rules.body: A glow is a state signal, never atmosphere. It appears only on elements that are actually live — a loaded runtime, a ready sandbox, the running mote. Adding a glow for warmth makes every real signal in the interface unreadable.

rules.name: The Inset Rule
rules.body: Selection and active state are a 1px inset cyan rule, never a fill. Fills at this density read as disabled surfaces; the rule reads as a marker.

rules.name: The Milled Panel Rule
rules.body: If it holds something, it is square. If you press it or type into it, it is 0.3rem. If it counts or reports, it is a pill. There is no fourth case.

rules.name: The Inline Confirmation Rule
rules.body: Destructive actions confirm in place, never through window.confirm. The control's own row becomes a confirmation strip — the question, a destructive confirm, a ghost cancel — bordered and washed in Alert Red. Reset does the same by swapping its own label to "Replace all files?" and reverting after 4 seconds or on blur. A modal dialog would block the tab and the automation harness both.

rules.name: The Readout Rule
rules.body: System state is always on screen, never behind a hover or a menu: sandbox readiness, console line and error counts, the origin guarantees, storage used, VRAM, tokens per second. The status bar's job is to make the machine's condition continuously legible.

dos: Do keep Signal Cyan to one meaning — live or selected — and to roughly one element per region. Everything else that needs to feel cyan uses Trace Cyan.
Do set font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on every changing number.
Do give every new scroll region min-height: 0 and every flexible grid track minmax(0, 1fr).
Do reach for color-mix(in oklch, <token>, transparent N%) to recede a border or fill. That is how this system makes a value quieter — not by introducing a new token.
Do confirm destructive actions inline, in the control's own row.
Do keep chrome heights aligned: 4rem top bars, 2.6rem section headers, 1.8rem status bar.
Do reserve monospace for code, logs, paths, and measurements.
Do test every UI change at ≤760px, where the shell stacks into two full-height screens.
donts: Don't introduce purple gradients, sparkles, robot or brain imagery, or friendly-assistant framing. This is a standing brand commitment from PRODUCT.md, not a style preference.
Don't add drop shadows. If something needs to separate, it takes a border or a tonal step.
Don't use a glow for atmosphere. A glow means the element is live.
Don't round a panel, a tool card, a code well, or a progress track. Structure is square.

Don't animate layout properties — width, height, padding, margin — on the load progress bar. The design detector hook blocks those writes, and the bar's inner span width is the one exception that is already accounted for.

Don't put Inter, or any other webfont, into the sandbox starter CSS. The host application keeps Inter; generated pages use a system stack, because they are a different world and because a sandboxed page cannot load fonts through the CSP.
Don't call window.confirm, alert, or prompt from the host or the sandbox. The sandbox runtime deliberately replaces all three with an in-page toast plus a console line.
Don't add a light theme or a theme toggle. color-scheme: dark is set at the root and the entire palette is built for it.
Don't use Alert Red for things that already happened, or Log Red on a control you can press.
